definitions.gloss: to take a shortcut; to cut through
definitions.explanation: To go by a shorter route than the usual one to save time or distance.

definitions.gloss: to take the easy way; to cut corners
definitions.explanation: To try to achieve something by an easier but possibly less thorough method.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}を{通|とお}って{近道|ちかみち}する。
examples.english: To take a shortcut through the park.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}がないから{近道|ちかみち}しよう。
examples.english: We don't have time, so let's take a shortcut.

examples.japanese: {裏道|うらみち}を{使|つか}って{近道|ちかみち}したら、{思|おも}ったより{早|はや}く{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I took a shortcut using the back streets and arrived earlier than expected.

examples.japanese: {勉強|べんきょう}に{近道|ちかみち}はない。
examples.english: There are no shortcuts to learning.

examples.japanese: {近道|ちかみち}しようとして{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: I tried to take a shortcut and failed.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}への{近道|ちかみち}は{地道|じみち}な{努力|どりょく}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that the shortcut to success is steady effort.

notes:
{近道|ちかみち} (shortcut) + する. The noun {近道|ちかみち} can stand alone (meaning a shorter path), and when combined with する, it becomes a verb meaning to take that shorter path.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {近道|ちかみち}を{通|とお}る — go via a shortcut
- {近道|ちかみち}はない — there are no shortcuts
- {成功|せいこう}への{近道|ちかみち} — shortcut to success
- {近道|ちかみち}を{教|おし}える — show someone a shortcut

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {抜|ぬ}け{道|みち} — back road; loophole — a hidden or lesser-known route; also means a way around rules
- {回|まわ}り{道|みち} — detour; roundabout way — the opposite: a longer route
